SingleBell is a slate, written on in chalk. It gives you one practice for the day,
counts it with you, and gets out of the way.

Native SwiftUI. No dependencies. No network code. No account.

[Coming to the App Store]{.pill}

::: {.shots}
![The day's practice, dealt fresh each morning](images/singlebell/home.png){group="shots"}

![Every card opens the board before it starts anything](images/singlebell/chalkboard.png){group="shots"}

![The clock counts, or you do](images/singlebell/clock-work.png){group="shots"}
:::

## What it does

**The day's practice.** One card each morning, dealt from the week's shape and what
you have already done — clean and press, one-arm swings, snatches — with its warm-up,
complex and finisher chalked on the board and an honest estimate of what it costs.
Choose short or standard. The day is dealt once and holds until midnight; finishing it
resolves the card in place rather than moving it under your feet.

**The classics, done properly.** Simple & Sinister, Quick and the Dead, Rite of
Passage, Armor Building, the Kettlebell Axe, the Humane Burpee and more — each one
credited to where it came from, each one adjustable on the slate before you start.

**A builder.** Make your own: complexes on the clock, the same complexes on a
whiteboard where you count the sets, or plain intervals. Keep what you make in Library.

**A reference.** Every move has a sheet — how it's done, what it's for, the cues that
matter. The get-up is never dealt to you automatically, because it is a skill before it
is a set.

**On the Lock Screen.** A running practice shows its round and its clock without
unlocking the phone. A home-screen widget carries the week's tally.

## What it deliberately doesn't do

No streaks. No badges. No confetti. No charts or stat dashboards. No social feed, no
followers, no sharing. No account. No ads. No motivational copy, and not one
exclamation mark anywhere in the app.

The absence is the point. A practice you keep is not one you were nagged into.

## Privacy {#privacy}

*Effective 28 August 2026.*

**SingleBell collects nothing.** Not anonymised, not aggregated, not "to improve the
experience". Nothing. The rest of this section is only the detail behind that sentence.

### Nothing leaves your phone

The app contains no networking code at all. It does not connect to a server, because
there is no server. There is no account to create, nothing to sign in to, and no way
for me — or anyone else — to see that you use the app, let alone what you do in it.

There are no analytics, no crash reporters, no advertising identifiers, no attribution
frameworks, and no third-party SDKs of any kind.

### It asks you for nothing

SingleBell requests no permissions. Not your location, contacts, photos, calendar,
microphone, camera, or Health data. It is not integrated with HealthKit. You will never
see a permission prompt, because the app declares none.

The coach's voice is your device's built-in speech synthesis — sound going out, never
sound coming in. Nothing is recorded and nothing is listened to. The app keeps audio
running in the background for one reason: so the count keeps speaking when your screen
locks mid-set.

The Lock Screen Live Activity is drawn on your device and updated by the app itself. It
uses no push token and no notification server.

### What is stored, and where

Your practice log, the sessions you save to Library, and your preferences are written
to your device's own storage, in a container shared only between SingleBell and its
own widgets — that sharing is what lets the home-screen widget show this week's tally.
That container is on your phone and nowhere else.

If your phone backs itself up to iCloud or to a computer, that backup will include
SingleBell's data exactly as it includes every other app's. Those backups are covered
by Apple's privacy policy, not by this one.

### Deleting it

Delete the app and everything goes with it. There is no copy held anywhere else and
nothing to request from me, because I never had it in the first place.

### Children

No data is collected from anyone, of any age.

### Changes

If any of this ever stops being true, this page will say so before the version that
changes it ships, and the date above will change.
